children: A deadly missile strike on Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid International Airport has intensified regional tensions, prompting President
Donald Trump
to consider joining Saudi military operations against Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.
Missile Attack on Riyadh Airport

Early Sunday, Saudi civil aviation authorities said that the latest attack on Riyadh’s international airport killed 12 people and injured more than 300, with some victims in critical condition, reported AP News.
The dead included a U.S. citizen and nationals of Saudi Arabia, Bangladesh, Egypt, Jordan, Palestine, Syria and Sudan.
A missile struck an airport complex housing terminals 3 and 4, which serve domestic flights, a regional official told The AP.
The Saudi authorities and the Saudi-led coalition blamed the Iran-backed Houthis for the attack, calling the strike a "fully-fledged war crime" and vowing a firm response.
The attack followed a series of Houthi strikes on Saudi airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure after a Saudi-led coalition launched a major offensive against the rebels.
Trump Weighs US Strikes Against Iran-Backed Houthis
On Saturday, Trump said he was considering U.S. involvement in Saudi strikes against the rebels.
"We may. We’re going to look at it," Trump told reporters. "We just found out about the recent attack. So we’ll make a decision. We move very quickly."
He later said he planned to speak with Saudi Crown Prince
Mohammed bin Salman
and said, "What happened in Saudi Arabia is not acceptable."
Secretary of State
Marco Rubio
condemned the strike after confirming an American citizen had been killed.
"These reprehensible attacks demonstrate a blatant disregard for innocent civilian life. They must stop now," he said.

The United States strongly condemns the recent attacks on the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia by the terrorist Houthis, including today’s strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that took numerous innocent lives, including an American citizen.
